paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So my goal is actually quite ambitious. It's an idea that I had many, many years ago, and I'm asking for your help as well. Not everyone — if you don't have to help — but I'm asking for the help.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So something weird happened. What happened to me was that I was in a yoga teacher training, and my teacher — who was a teacher from our lineage — whispered in my ear (this is like weekend two or three of yoga teacher training; I'm doing down dogs, learning some theory), and he says, "You know, there's this thing in November called Lam Rim." And I was like, "What?" I heard the words. I didn't know what they meant, but I heard the words, and they resonated inside me almost like a bakchak [BAG CHAGS] {? sepa} — like some kind of seed went off. And he said, "You should go. I think you'd like it." So I flew across the country.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I have no idea what I'm getting myself into. And I don't think any of you really know what you're getting yourself into. So I'm going to tell you what you're getting yourself into, and then you can just cancel — just leave the meeting if you're not into it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So I show up, and I'm thinking Lam Rim is this thing — okay, it's a 10-day teaching. It was sold as a 10-day teaching with a 10-day meditation retreat afterwards. I'm like, "Oh, cool. I could do that. Not a problem. I'm working for myself. I'll take the 10 days off, 20 days off." So I fly across the country. I fly to Phoenix, Arizona. And some weird seeds are going off. We're sitting in these classes, and I'm listening, and I realize — oh, see, two people just left, they're done — I'm listening, and all of a sudden I realize this is not a 20-day course. It was sold as a 10-year course. It was like, "Oh, we're going to do the entire book over the next 10 years." And I'm sitting there and I'm like, "Okay, bring it on. Fine. We're doing this." And something shifted in me in this very deep way.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So after the class is over, I flew home. I was living on the East Coast of the United States, living in Philadelphia at the time. And I'm on the airplane, and all of a sudden my mind goes, "What the hell? You just committed to 10 years of your life. You can't commit to a three-month relationship. You break up with people after three months because you can't handle the fire. You just committed to 10 years of your life. What the hell are you doing, Tim?" And I was like, "I don't know." I'd laugh at that, but I never questioned it. I never questioned what I saw as the potential to change myself and to change the world.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So there's been 45 Lam Rims. That's a lot. Let's go back to the beginning and start. Let's just start again. Geshe Michael was taught it three times. I've read the book a billion times. It's a phenomenal guide to how to live a better life and how to help other people, period. It's not Buddhism. It's not any of this. It is just how to live a better life and how to take care of other people, period. And if that's something that's interesting to you, then let's do this.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now, what do I need help with? I realized pretty close to the beginning — I always want to show you a picture from way back in the beginning. This was really cool. Way back in the beginning, there was this guy named Scott Vasek, wonderful man. He ran DCI for many, many years. And Scott Vasek had the vision — just like John Stilwell had the vision — to record all the ACI courses. And he was like, "We need to record all the Lam Rims. We need a recording of all of this. We cannot not have this." So here's Scott. And Scott taught me the value of having records.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then I realized that we're going to have 20 years — well, now it's 20 years — of courses. And video is not as accessible a thing; no one's going to watch 20 years of courses. And I had this vision that we should translate Pabongka Rinpoche's Lam Rim from Geshe Michael's commentary — that we should publish books, just like Trijang Rinpoche did, who spent much of his life recording and making accessible, for future generations, Pabongka's teachings. And I think we should do the same thing with Geshe Michael's teachings. He added in a tremendous amount of commentary and resources to the Lam Rim that's not included in Pabongka's text — a lot of commentary that I think we should not only translate, but also publish.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So part of this course — this is a whole long introduction, I know we only have an hour — this course will be a translation course as well, of Pabongka's Lam Rim. We're going to be going through the text, and I'm going to be doing the best that I can. I've been studying this for 14 years. I've been officially translating texts for about two years now, being trained to do it. And I need your help. Let's translate this together. If you're not interested in translating, that's okay, just come to the classes. If you're not interested in Tibetan, I don't care, just say the words — do the "blah, blah." Eventually the words sink into your head. But if you want to help with the translation, let's do it. Because we have different perspectives on it, and Geshe-la has different perspectives, and even Art Engle had a different perspective. Neither is correct or incorrect, but they're different perspectives. And I think we should publish them, and take the time to study it and practice it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That's the thing — to be a good translator, you have to be a practitioner, and you have to practice the teachings. You have to put them into practice, so you understand what it says. You could just do the words, and just know the Tibetan. But if you know the words as lived experience — your personal experience in the Lam Rim, in the stories in your life, because you saw the Lam Rim out there, you saw it as a living example, you saw it in your own life...

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: You want to see the Lam Rim? Turn on CNN. Turn on the news. Bombs, planes exploding, people dying all the time. It's right there. You want to see Lam Rim? It's not very far away. You want to see Lam Rim? Watch your mind. Watch the stuff that goes on in your mind throughout the day when people say or do things to you that you think are coming from them — and it looks like they're coming from them, and it's functionally coming from them — and then you have all your emotional reactions to it. And then how do you help? How do you help yourself in that? And how do you help others? How do you live it? That's why we're calling it Living Lam Rim. How are you living this? Because to be a translator, you have to be a living practitioner.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm a good translator, I would say. And we're going to take Geshe-la's oral translations and publish the books, and hopefully we'll have enough time with Geshe Michael to get his feedback on everything. So we're just going to take our time. We're going to be patient with it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: What I'm planning on doing is: we're going to go through some text in each class, and then we'll send it to you guys. And those of you that want to learn how to translate, you can send them back — send in your homework, and I'll read it, and then we'll put together a group translation. And for those of you that aren't fluent in English — good, it'll help you become fluent in English. For those of you that want to then translate all of this into your own language — great, you'll learn the Lam Rim, you'll live the Lam Rim, we'll have an English translation, and then you'll translate it into your own language. If you know Spanish really well, Sandra, maybe you'll translate it into Spanish after we've done it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And the idea is — we're not going to take 20 years to publish the thing. We're going to publish it in pieces. So piece number one, in my mind — we'll see if it actually agrees or not — piece number one will be the meditation and wisdom chapters together. We'll do the two of those and publish that one book. So then people have that right away. Let's not wait 20 years so people can learn to meditate. And then you have the responsibility to go out and teach it. You teach people meditation. You teach people emptiness. You start teaching them Lam Rim. And then, piece by piece, we'll create it together.

chapters.title: Reading the title — "Liberation in the Palm of Your Hand"

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So we have five minutes. I prepared a huge class that I didn't get to. As you guys can see, this is everything I prepared for today. We have four minutes. Thank you for joining.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So, day 21. Here's the beginning of day 21 — ninyer-chik-par [„NYIN NYER GCIG PAR,] — on folio 345A. It's near the end of 345 of about 400. We're going to go to the very beginning — we're going to the first folio, folio one — and this is the title. We're going to get the first part and then we're going to go. Here's the primary title. And I would like Anastasiia to read this part, please. Turn on your microphone.

paragraphs.speaker: Anastasiia
paragraphs.text: [RNAM GROL LAG BCANGS]

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: This is the primary title of the book. [RNAM GROL] is liberation. [LAG] is the palm of your hand. So this book, for short, we call it "the gift of liberation." This book is called "liberation thrust — put into the palm of your hand." Everyone extend your left hand, put your palm out. And then someone goes, "Here you go," and they shove it in your hand. They close the palm up and they're like, "Here's your liberation." And this title is not used anywhere else. There's no other book called this, as far as I know. It's "Liberation Thrust into the Palm of Your Hand." Someone is putting it into your hand.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then the other part of the title, which we'll go through really quickly and then we'll finish this paragraph next time, is right here. {\~ Discipling Poem} The other title is "The Essence of Deathless Nectar" — the essence of deathlessness. Those two things together: here's your hand, this book will place it — it's almost like a slap, like, "I'm going to put this in your hand, and there you go, now you have it. Close your hand. And now you have the essence of deathlessness, right here from the beginning of this book." And that's what this book is set up to do.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: [RNAM GROL LAG BCANGS] — everybody knows what that means. That's the short title. This is the common title: "Liberation Thrust into the Palm of Your Hand." More gently, we say "the gift of liberation." It's a gift given to you, into the palm of your hand — your extended hand. You're asking. There's an ask. You are opening yourself to it. You're opening your heart. You're opening your hands. You're opening your mind. You're asking for it. And then here it is: you ask for it, here it is, here's the way to do it, here are all the steps. So welcome to the rest of your life.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: There's a lot here. I'm really happy. There are 184 people here. I'm really surprised. This is amazing. This is also part of helping ensure that we continue to have Lam Rim, that we can continue to get the teachings.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We have 5% left in this book. We have another six years of the Lam Rim Chenmo — by 2030 is when this is all expected to be done. The other part of what we're going to be doing, part of the ending of 2030, is also going to include 100 meditations from the Lam Rim that will be delivered from ACI, from Geshe Michael. And the idea behind all of this is to honor the lineage. It's not honoring one person. It's honoring the lineage of people that have brought this to us — from Je Tsongkapa through Pabongka Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Lobsang Tharchin, Geshe Lobsang Chunzin, and then us here. We have that lineage.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So that's what we're going to be doing each week. We'll be slowly going through the text. We're not going to have any homework this week, because we had five words. But I'll be sending it out each week, and then you can send it on and send back what you think the translation is. It'll help you out a ton. You'll probably learn how much you need to learn. And we'll go through it bit by bit. And I promise, over time, these things and ideas become second nature — especially when you're having a challenging moment and you do the thing that is the most powerful and the kindest thing that can happen. That's when you know you have success. That's when you know you've become someone who really can change and help other people.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So no, you don't need to know any Tibetan. If you're brand new, just try. Some people here can help you with resources. You don't have to do the translation — you can just come to the class. It's not an obligatory thing. Anyone who does help with the translation, you will get a byline in the book. We'll have like 10 pages of names of all the people that helped.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm going to just be sending the ACIP input. I'm not going to be sending the script. At some later point, we'll start putting the script up so you guys can learn that too, because you need to learn how to read Tibetan as Tibetan really is. But we're going to be doing it from the ACIP input.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So thank you all for joining. Happy New Year. Happy 2024. There are a lot of people here who I don't know. I'm very happy to see new faces. I'm happy you're here. If you have any questions, don't hesitate to reach out. My Telegram is this — you can find me there. I take time to respond sometimes. Do not translate with AI. You are learning to be a human translator. We'll talk about AI later. Thank you all very much for joining. Hope to see you next week. And happy 2024. Turn on your microphones and say goodbye to everyone.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Thank you. Thank you, teacher Tim.
